brief:
Israel's relations with Western allies have deteriorated sharply over escalating violence in the occupied West Bank, compounding friction already created by its conduct in the Gaza war, according to Al-Monitor. The diplomatic friction arrives at a critical juncture, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government facing mounting criticism from traditional partners as the country heads toward close-fought October elections.

The timing of the West Bank tensions intersects with a closely contested domestic political race, adding pressure on Netanyahu as he navigates both international scrutiny and electoral competition at home. Western governments have grown increasingly vocal about their concerns regarding Israeli operations in the territory.

title: Israel strains Western ties with West Bank violence before elections
